neighbours.label: something false, fake or hollow ('obviously fake', 'the wrong thing', 'empty promises'); the output promotes ' false', ' fake', ' mock', ' dummy'
fire: Police say the seller used a fake passport at the border.
That email is an obviously false claim about your account.
Sometimes people say the wrong thing at a funeral.
Voters are tired of empty promises from every party.
The forger printed fake banknotes in his cellar.
This website spreads false rumors about the vaccine.
My cousin took the wrong train to the airport.
Those are hollow threats from a weak government.
quiet: At the border an agent checked a real passport carefully.
Your account has a correct balance, the email says.
Friends often say kind things at a funeral.
Every party made firm plans for its voters.
In his cellar the banker stored genuine banknotes.
Accurate reports about the vaccine appear on this website.
Our train to the airport left on time.
A strong government kept its word on trade.

notes: Card: ' fake' x3, ',' x3, ' wrong' x2, ' false' x2, ' for' x2; promotes ' false', ' fake', ' mock', ' dummy', ' useless', ' meaningless'. Probe: ' promises' after 'empty' 0.680; ' fake' 0.402-0.519; ' wrong' 0.352; ' real' sentence 0.006; 'right thing' sentence 0.024. The 'p <' and Chinese comma peaks are not covered. Near misses are true or real things, with other openings.
